I've added automerge for minor and patch updates, and for lockfile maintenance, to `renovate.json`. It's uncommitted on `main`, and I haven't run Renovate against the repo.

```json
"lockFileMaintenance": { "enabled": true, "automerge": true },
"packageRules": [
  {
    "description": "Automerge minor and patch updates once CI passes; majors still need a human",
    "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch"],
    "automerge": true
  },
  ...existing rules
]
```

- **Lockfile updates:** `config:best-practices` doesn't turn on `lockFileMaintenance` by default, so I enabled it explicitly (it runs weekly, before 4am on Mondays by default). That refreshes `uv.lock` in its own PR, and I set it to automerge.
- **Rule order:** The new automerge rule comes first, so your existing rules still override it. The disabled `uv-pre-commit` and `python` rules stay disabled, and the ruff group still moves together.
- **Gate:** Automerge uses Renovate's default of waiting for passing status checks. Your `ruff`, `tools-tests` and `firmware-tests` checks have to be required (or at least pass) before anything merges.
- **Validation:** The validator I could fetch is Renovate 37, and it rejects the existing `github-actions.managerFilePatterns` option as too new. That error comes from your existing config, not my changes, and my additions raised no errors. I haven't checked the file with the current Renovate version.

# Linear tracking

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

## Filing issues

- Every issue gets the `stopwatch-screensaver` label (in the `Repo` group) and exactly
  one label from the `Work Type` group. The group is single-select, so
  pick the one that fits best (see below).
- Always set a priority (Urgent, High, Medium, Low). Never leave it at
  "No priority".
- Link the draft trail or spec section if one exists. Copy the body from
  `entire trail show N --json`; `entire trail list --json` returns empty
  bodies.

## Choosing a Work Type

| Label         | Use it for                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Bug`         | Fixing something that isn't operating correctly. |
| `Feature`     | Adding new functionality to the app.             |
| `Enhancement` | Improving existing functionality.                |
| `Performance` | Improving the performance of code.               |
| `Chore`       | Maintenance, tooling and documentation work.     |

Several of these can fit one ticket. Decide by asking these in order and
taking the first yes:

1. Does the app do something other than what was intended? `Bug`, even if
   the symptom is slowness or the fix is a refactor.
1. Is the behaviour right, but too slow or heavy, and is speed or
   resource use the point of the work? `Performance`.
1. Does it give the user a capability they did not have? `Feature`.
1. Does it make a capability they already have better? `Enhancement`.
1. Does it change nothing a user would notice? `Chore`.

A ticket that bundles small, unrelated tidy-ups takes `Chore`. If the
bundle is mostly one other type, either split it or use that type.
Refactors, test additions, dependency bumps, build scripts, CI and
documentation are `Chore` unless they fix a defect.

## Status names

Use these exactly as Linear spells them: `Backlog`, `Todo`,
`In Progress`, `In Review`, `Done`, `Canceled`, `Duplicate`.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/.claude/skills/deliver-branch

# Delivering a branch

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- `entire trail create --title ... --type feature --body ...` pushes the branch
  (`--type` takes only `bug`, `feature` or `task`; `chore` is refused)
  and opens a linked DRAFT PR. The PR body is not synced from the trail: update
  both (`entire trail update --body`, `gh pr edit N --body-file`). Put
  `Fixes #N` in the body, then read the PR back (`gh pr view N --json body`):
  #27 merged with the generic body, so `Fixes #23` never reached GitHub and
  the issue stayed open until it was closed by hand.
- Rod approves and merges (merge commit). Afterwards delete the merged branch
  (remote and local) without asking and fast-forward `main`. Confirm the merge
  after a fresh `git fetch`: a stale `origin/main` says "not merged". Remove
  the branch's worktree first (a checked-out branch cannot be deleted), and
  note that `git branch -d` refuses while local `main` is behind, so check
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main` and then use `-D`. `main` is
  usually checked out in Rod's main checkout, so `git fetch origin main:main`
  is refused there: run `git merge --ff-only origin/main` in it, only if
  `git status` shows no tracked changes.
- Merge with `gh pr ready N` then `entire trail merge <trail>` (the trail
  number, not the PR number; omit it on the trail's branch) once Rod approves
  (trail PRs are drafts). `entire trail merge` checks the gates first and
  merges nothing while one fails or is pending; `--dry-run` reports which.
  Rod's approval is enough: do not wait for the Entire Gates check to finish.
  If the only failing gates are Approvals (he approved in chat) or a stacked
  PR's "Up to date: 1 commit behind" once its parent merges, and the PR is
  mergeable, try `entire trail merge <trail> --force --yes` with no rebase;
  the bypass is recorded on the trail. The repo's bypass policy is now
  "nobody", so it is refused ("does not allow bypassing gates", PR #132):
  do not merge round it with `gh pr merge`. Ask Rod to approve the trail in
  the Entire UI, then run a plain `entire trail merge`. For any other failing
  gate, stop and tell Rod.
- Before merging, `git fetch` and compare the PR's `headRefOid` with your tip:
  Rod sometimes pushes to the branch (docs commits, a merge of `main`). Read
  what arrived with `git log --oneline <tip>..origin/<branch>`, and clean up
  from the merge commit, not your last push. After `ExitWorktree keep` the
  tool names the branch `worktree-<name>`; the real branch is
  `git worktree list`'s.
- A trail's "N commits behind" can understate: trail 66 said 1 and its branch
  was 17 behind. Count with `git rev-list --count <branch>..origin/main`
  before a cherry-pick, and re-apply by hand if the files conflict.
- To read another agent's session, run `entire checkpoint explain <checkpoint>
  --full` (or `--transcript` for the JSONL) from the repo root: elsewhere it
  says "not a git repository". `entire session info <id>` knows only local
  sessions, so find the checkpoint with `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` on
  one of the agent's commits.
- A review of fixed code can raise a new finding on the fix itself (a clamp
  that did not stop a wrap). Reproduce it with a failing test before changing
  the code, and mutation-check each branch of the new guard.
- Write a PR body to a file for `gh pr edit --body-file` (an apostrophe in an
  inline `--body '...'` must be `'"'"'`).
- `gh pr edit N --body-file` replaces the whole body, including the
  `<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->` ... `-end -->` block at the top. Keep that
  block in the file, or the PR loses its trail.
- Findings: `entire trail finding list N`, then `... resolve N <id> -m "..."`.
  Bot reviews can lag about 20 minutes. `N` is the trail number (PR #12 was
  trail 6), not the PR number. For a false positive or upstream behaviour in a
  byte-identical hack, use `entire trail finding dismiss N <id> -m "<reason>"`.
- To file your own review's findings: `entire trail finding add --trail N
  --client-id <key> --severity high|medium|low --file <path> --start-line A
  --end-line B -m "<body>"` (no title flag; the client id makes a re-run safe).
  Open the body by saying an agent filed it for Rod.
- In a worktree session create the trail with a one-line `--body`, then set the
  real body with `gh pr edit N --body-file` (keep the trail-link block), and
  check `closingIssuesReferences` with `gh pr view N --json` (it can lag a
  few seconds).
- `entire trail update --body` takes no number and acts on the current
  branch (`entire trail update 8` errors).
- Stacked PR: `entire trail create --base <parent-branch>`. When the parent
  merges, `gh pr edit N --base main` before deleting its branch, then
  `git rebase --onto origin/main <old parent tip>`. The rebased push needs
  `--force-with-lease` (ask Rod first), unless the branch was never pushed.
- `docs/porting-assessment.md` conflicts on rebase: `git checkout --theirs`
  it to continue, then rerun `tools/score_hacks.py` and amend the result in.
- Two ports in flight both append to `g_hacks[]`, so whichever merges second
  conflicts in `registry.c`, the expected list in `test_hacks.c`,
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `tools/assessment_measured.md.in` (rows,
  paragraphs and the hack count) and the three `build_src_filter` lines in `platformio.ini`,
  as well as the generated assessment. Keep both sides, put the newer hack
  last, and regenerate the assessment. A rebased published branch needs
  `--force-with-lease` (ask Rod), and GitHub can reject that push once too.
- A finding that says the code "does not exist" can be stale after a rebase
  (the skill PR was reviewed before the Blaster and Substrate code it referred
  to had landed). Check it against `main` before dismissing, and put the
  evidence in the dismissal. Entire's approvals gate once showed "no reviewers
  have approved" right after a force push, though Rod had approved; his word is
  enough, so say so and go ahead.
- `entire trail finding list` can show one open "Review verdict ... approve"
  finding: it is the reviewers' verdict, not a defect. `mergeStateStatus`
  reads UNSTABLE while the gate runs, and Rod's approval is enough.
- A shared-code PR (stroker, runner, canvas) can move pins of hacks merged
  since it branched: merge or rebase onto `main` and rerun the pin loop before
  judging frames (Celtic joined #89's moved set after #88 landed).
- Why a gate is red: `gh api
  repos/rodbegbie/stopwatch-screensaver/commits/<branch>/check-runs
  --jq '.check_runs[]|.output.summary'`.
  "Approvals: failed" is just Rod not having approved yet, and "Checks:
  skipped" is normal (no CI here). `entire trail watch` streams forever, so to
  watch poll `gh pr view N`, that API and `entire trail finding list N` from a
  script file under a Monitor, printing only on change. Merge only when Rod
  says to, even once the gates are green.
- If `entire trail create` reports "failed to push branch", run
  `git push -u origin <branch>` and rerun it: the trail is then created.
- Run `gh pr ready N` and `entire trail merge <trail>` as separate commands:
  on a PR that is already ready, `ready` exits non-zero and skips a chained
  merge.
  Confirm with `gh pr view N --json state`.
- `entire trail merge <trail> --dry-run` can say "findings pending: Waiting
  for the agent review of the current head" with "bypass policy (nobody)".
  Rod merging `main` into the branch makes a new head and the review runs
  again (it cleared in under 20 minutes). `--force` is refused: poll the dry
  run from a script under a Monitor, then merge when it reads "Mergeable:
  yes". First `git fetch`, compare the PR's `headRefOid` with the tip, and
  check `finding list --status open`.

## Linear: creating the trail

After Rod approves creating it, do all three steps together:

1. Start the trail body with `Linear: ARS-NN` and the ticket URL, so a
   reader of the trail can reach the ticket.
1. Run `entire trail create`, then comment the trail URL on the ticket.
1. Set the ticket to **In Review**.

If a draft trail already exists for the work, link it in the new trail's
body. A draft trail has no branch and cannot be attached to one, so the
new trail supersedes it; tell Rod so he can close the draft.

## Linear: after the merge

When Rod says the trail is approved: run `entire trail merge N --dry-run`,
merge it, fast-forward local `main`, and delete the merged branch locally
and on origin. Then set the ticket to **Done**. If the merge fails or Rod
asks for changes, set the ticket back to **In Progress**.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/.claude/skills/address-findings

# Address Findings

Fix and resolve the open review findings on an Entire trail. A finding is a
review comment posted to a trail on entire.io: it has a file/line location, a
body, a severity, and sometimes a suggested unified-diff patch. This skill
fetches the open findings, applies or hand-fixes each one in the current
worktree, and marks it resolved on the trail.

## When to use / not use

Use when the user points at a trail — a URL like
`https://<host>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<number>/<slug>`, or a bare trail
number or branch — and asks to **address / fix / resolve** its findings or
review comments.

Do **not** use this skill for:

- A code review of the current diff — that is the `review` skill (read-only).
- Creating new findings — use `entire trail finding add`.

## Response Format

Begin the first response to this skill invocation with the line:

`Entire Address Findings:`

followed by a blank line, then the content. Apply the header to the **first
response only**. Omit it on error / early-exit responses (CLI missing, not
authenticated, trail not found, branch mismatch, no open findings).

## Rules

1. Make the smallest correct change that addresses each finding. Do not expand scope.
2. Only mark a finding resolved when you actually addressed it. If a finding is
   ambiguous or needs a human decision, leave it open and report it.
3. Do not commit or push. Leave changes in the working tree for the user to review.
4. Never weaken a test or assertion just to clear a finding.

## Process

### 1. Verify the CLI

Run `entire version`. If the command is not found, stop and tell the user:
"The Entire CLI is required but not installed. Install it from
https://entire.io/docs/cli and try again."

### 2. Resolve the trail selector

- If the argument is a trail URL, take the number from the `/trails/<number>/`
  path segment and use that number.
- If it is a bare trail number, id, or branch name, use it as-is.
- If you cannot determine a trail, stop and ask the user for the trail URL or number.

Use this value as the `<trail>` selector for every command below. `entire trail`
accepts a trail number, id, or branch name interchangeably, so no number lookup
is needed — a branch name works directly.

### 3. Fetch open findings

```bash
entire trail finding list <trail> --json --status open
```

- If the output reports that authentication is required, stop and tell the user:
  "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- If the `trail finding` subcommand is unavailable, or the API reports the
  feature is not enabled, stop and tell the user that trail findings may not be
  enabled for this account or repository. Do not invent findings.
- Parse the JSON. Each finding has an id, a severity, a status, a body, a
  location (file path + line range), and may include a suggested change (a
  unified diff).
- If there are no open findings, report "No open findings on this trail." and stop.

### 4. Branch guard (you must be on the trail's branch)

`entire trail finding apply` edits the local worktree, so you must be on the
trail's branch before changing files.

```bash
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD                # current branch
entire trail list --json --status any -n 200   # locate the trail's branch
```

Find the trail whose `number` or `branch` matches your selector and read its `branch`.

- If the trail's branch differs from the current branch, stop and tell the user:
  "Trail `<trail>` targets branch `<trail-branch>`, but you are on
  `<current-branch>`. Check it out first (`entire trail checkout <trail>`) and
  re-run." Do not edit files.
- If you cannot find the trail in the list (e.g. pagination), do not hard-fail:
  warn that you could not verify the branch, and ask the user to confirm they are
  on the trail's branch before you continue.

### 5. Address each finding

Process findings highest severity first (high → medium → low). For each:

1. **If it has a suggested unified-diff change**, dry-run it first:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --check
   ```

   If it applies cleanly, apply and resolve in one step:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --resolve
   ```

2. **Otherwise** (no patch, the patch conflicts, or the fix needs reasoning):
   read the finding body, open the file at its location, and make the smallest
   correct edit that addresses it. If a fast, relevant local check exists for the
   touched code (a build or a focused test), run it. Then resolve:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding resolve <trail> <finding-id> -m "<one line: what you changed>"
   ```

3. **If you cannot confidently address it** (ambiguous, needs a product/design
   decision, or out of scope): leave it open, do not resolve it, and record it
   for the report.

### 6. Report

Summarize:

- Resolved via suggested patch — list finding ids and files.
- Resolved via manual edit — list finding ids, files, and a one-line of what changed.
- Left open for your decision — list finding ids and why.
- Any errors encountered.

Remind the user the changes are uncommitted and ready for review.

## Failure modes

- **CLI not installed** → install message (step 1).
- **Not authenticated** → "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- **Trail findings not enabled / API error** → tell the user the feature may be
  unavailable; do not fabricate findings.
- **Trail not found** → tell the user to check the URL or number; suggest
  `entire trail list --status any`.
- **Wrong branch** → stop with the checkout instruction (step 4).
- **Patch does not apply** → fall back to a manual edit; if you cannot fix it
  confidently, leave the finding open and report it.
- **Not a git repository** → stop and tell the user to run from inside the trail's repo.

content.text:
Entire Address Findings:

I resolved one of the two findings and left the other open for your call. The `minimumReleaseAge` change is uncommitted in `renovate.json`.

**Resolved: medium (`01M5ZD4R…`), no age gate on automerge**
- I added `"minimumReleaseAge": "3 days"` to the minor/patch automerge rule, as you chose.
- The repo's `renovate-config-validator` pre-commit hook passes.
- **Lockfile gap:** I did not add the age gate to `lockFileMaintenance`. Lockfile maintenance has no per-release timestamps for it to check, so the setting wouldn't do anything there. Those PRs still run weekly and automerge, so a hijacked transitive release can be pulled in without a 3-day wait. The finding's other suggestion would close that gap: stop automerging lockfile maintenance, or restrict automerge to `matchManagers: ["pep621"]`.
- **Digest updates:** The finding also says SHA-pinned actions and pre-commit revs count as patch bumps, so they are automerged. That contradicts what I wrote earlier ("digest and pin updates stay manual"). They're now covered by the 3-day wait, but my PR and trail descriptions are wrong on this point.

**Left open: low (`01M5ZD49…`), pre-commit hooks automerge on a CI that doesn't run them**
- CI only runs ruff and `ty` from the pre-commit set. A minor bump of markdownlint, gitleaks or `validate-pyproject` could merge on a green CI that never ran it.
- The two fixes are excluding `matchManagers: ["pre-commit"]` (except ruff) from automerge, or adding `pre-commit run --all-files` to CI. That's a product decision, so I didn't pick one.

Decisions for you:
1. **Pre-commit:** exclude pre-commit hooks from automerge (my pick), or run the full hook set in CI?
2. **Lockfile maintenance:** keep it automerging, or make it manual?

Once you've answered, I'll commit and push, and fix the "digest updates stay manual" lines in the ARS-72 ticket, the PR and the trail.

1. Keep the pre-commit hooks in automerge -- run the full hook set in CI.
2. Keep it automerging.

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  UV_VERSION: "0.13.5"
  PYTHON_VERSION: "3.13.14"
  XSCREENSAVER_VERSION: "6.17"

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-python: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - run: uv run --locked ruff check
      - run: uv run --locked ruff format --check
      - run: uv run --locked ty check

  tools-tests:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-python: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .cache/xscreensaver
          key: xscreensaver-${{ env.XSCREENSAVER_VERSION }}
      - name: Fetch xscreensaver
        run: |
          uv run --locked tools/fetch_xscreensaver.py \
            --version "$XSCREENSAVER_VERSION" \

      - name: Use clang as cc
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang
          sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/cc cc /usr/bin/clang 100

      - run: uv run --locked pytest tools/tests --junitxml=reports/pytest.xml

        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-python: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
